title: State Department UAP Cable 1, Papua New Guinea, January 28, 1985

key_claims: PNG National Intelligence Organization received reports of high-altitude, high-speed aircraft over PNG airspace on the evening of January 24, 1985, including sightings by local residents and an Air Niugini pilot whose radar detected aircraft flying south to north at high altitude and high speed near Angoram.
Visual sightings of contrails were reported from various points around PNG: one aircraft moving north to south at 1900 local and six to eight aircraft traveling south to north at 2200 local.
The U.S. Embassy confirmed to PNG intelligence that it knew of no B-52 overflights and no U.S. aircraft in PNG airspace on January 24, 1985.
Local residents in Wewak were frightened by the overflights, prompting the provincial premier to call a public meeting attended by the Prime Minister.
The Embassy requested USCINCPAC confirmation that no U.S. aircraft were responsible and any additional information on the reports.
novelty_signals: Radar detection by a civilian airline pilot corroborating ground-based visual sightings of contrails and lights
Multiple objects reported: six to eight aircraft in formation traveling south to north
Foreign government intelligence service formally querying the U.S. Embassy about unidentified aerial phenomena
Public meeting called by provincial premier with Prime Minister in attendance due to civilian alarm over overflights
parsed.summary: A January 28, 1985 U.S. Embassy cable from Port Moresby reports that Papua New Guinea's National Intelligence Organization inquired about high-altitude, high-speed unidentified aircraft observed over PNG on the evening of January 24, 1985, including radar detection by an Air Niugini pilot and multiple visual sightings of contrails from various locations. The Embassy confirmed no known U.S. aircraft were in PNG airspace that night and requested USCINCPAC provide any information that might explain the reports.

title: State Department UAP Cable 2, Kazakhstan, January 31, 1994

key_claims: On January 27, 1994, a Tajik Air crew of one Tajik pilot and three American citizens encountered a UAP while flying a Boeing 747SP at 41,000 feet over Kazakhstan at coordinates 45N 55E.

The object appeared as a bright light of enormous intensity approaching from the eastern horizon at great speed and much higher altitude, maneuvering in circles, corkscrews, and 90-degree turns under very high G-forces for approximately 40 minutes.

The crew flew under contrails left by the object approximately 45 minutes after the initial sighting, with the contrails estimated at approximately 100,000 feet altitude — too high for ordinary aircraft propulsion to create contrails.
The crew, experienced former PanAm pilots, rejected the meteor hypothesis and expressed the opinion that the object was extraterrestrial and under intelligent control.
The light emitted had a 'bow wave' resembling a high-speed photograph of a bullet in flight, with a very small object giving off a much larger trailing wave of heat/light.
novelty_signals: Contrails observed at approximately 100,000 feet, far exceeding conventional aircraft ceiling
90-degree turns and corkscrew maneuvers at extreme speed implying forces incompatible with known aerodynamics
Experienced commercial airline pilots (former PanAm) as witnesses with explicit rejection of conventional explanations
Cable distributed to CIA WASHDC and DIA WASHDC indicating intelligence community interest
Diplomatic cable format — unusual channel for UAP reporting — from US Embassy in Dushanbe
parsed.summary: A US Department of State diplomatic cable from the embassy in Dushanbe reports that on January 27, 1994, a Tajik Air crew including American chief pilot Ed Rhodes observed a UAP while flying a 747SP at 41,000 feet over Kazakhstan, describing a bright light performing high-G maneuvers including 90-degree turns and corkscrews at extreme altitude. The experienced former PanAm crew estimated the object's contrails at approximately 100,000 feet and stated their belief that the object was extraterrestrial and under intelligent control.

title: State Department UAP Cable 3, Tbilisi, Georgia, October 30, 2001

key_claims: Deputy Foreign Minister Mamedov categorically denied that Russian planes were involved in any incidents over Georgian airspace on October 28-29, 2001, citing the Russian Ministry of Defense.

MFA Georgia Desk Chief Tereoken suggested that reports of planes over the Kodori Gorge might as well have been about UFOs, claiming Moscow lacked the technical capability to determine whether foreign planes were in the region.
Ambassador Vershbow warned that continued Russian airspace violations could be disastrous for U.S.-Russian relations and spoil the upcoming presidential summit.

The cable authors assess that Russian official denials reflect a traditional Russian penchant to avoid an awkward admission with a bold lie, and that Russia likely bombed the Kodori Gorge to pressure Georgians and Chechens.
Russia was using its 600 troops at Gudauta as a bargaining chip to extract concessions from Tbilisi on both the Boden Paper on Abkhazia and on clamping down on Chechens inside Georgia.
novelty_signals: UFO reference is not a genuine UAP sighting but a sarcastic Russian diplomatic deflection to deny responsibility for military airspace violations
Document illustrates state actors invoking UFOs as deliberate disinformation to obscure conventional military operations
Cable title 'Strange Encounters of an MFA Kind' is a sardonic play on 'Close Encounters of the Third Kind', signaling the authors did not take the UFO claim seriously
parsed.summary: This 2001 confidential State Department cable from the U.S. Embassy in Moscow reports that Russian officials denied Georgian accusations of Russian aircraft bombing the Kodori Gorge, with the MFA Georgia desk chief dismissively suggesting the unidentified aircraft could have been UFOs. The cable authors assess the UFO deflection as a characteristic Russian bold lie to conceal actual military operations intended to pressure Georgia over Chechens and the Abkhazia conflict.

title: State Department UAP Cable 4, Ashgabat, Turkmenistan, November 5, 2004

key_claims: The Union of UFOlogists of Turkmenabat, originally founded to study extraterrestrial life, became one of the USG's most reliable NGO partners in Turkmenistan for civil society work including business registration, humanitarian aid, and NGO capacity building.

UOU President Muradov stated that Turkmen military and government authorities had consulted him about mysterious occurrences in Turkmen airspace, but there had been no confirmed UFO sightings in Turkmenistan.
The UOU was the first NGO to register after Turkmenistan's independence in 1992 and the first to successfully re-register under the restrictive 2003 NGO law.
The UOU planned to publish 999 copies of an independent newsletter to stay below the 1000-copy threshold requiring a license, circumventing Turkmenistan's ban on independent media printing.
The UOU had over 1000 members and at least nine member organizations, and during the 1990s assisted 187 enterprises in registering with local authorities pro bono.
novelty_signals: A UFO-themed NGO used as a civil society vehicle in an authoritarian state, leveraging universal curiosity about UFOs to maintain good relations with local authorities.
Turkmen military consulted the UOU president about mysterious airspace occurrences, though no confirmed sightings resulted.
The cable's author endorses the UFO organization as 'crazy like a fox' and worthy of USG support, an unusual editorial stance in diplomatic correspondence.
parsed.summary: This 2004 State Department cable from Ashgabat describes the Union of UFOlogists of Turkmenabat, an NGO originally founded to study extraterrestrial life that evolved into one of the USG's most effective civil society partners in Turkmenistan, assisting with business registration, humanitarian aid distribution, and NGO capacity building. The cable's author notes with amusement that the organization's UFO branding gave it unique access and credibility with local authorities in the restrictive Turkmen environment, calling it 'crazy like a fox' and recommending continued USG support.

title: State Department UAP Cable 5, Mexico, September 16, 2003

organisations: Mexico City Secretariat of Citizen Security
White House Office of the Vice President
London School of Economics and Political Science
key_claims: The Mexican Congress heard testimony on UAP on September 12, 2003, debating language in the Aerial Space Protection Law that would make Mexico the first country to formally acknowledge the presence of alien life on Earth.
Experts including journalist Jaime Maussan and former U.S. Navy pilot Ryan Graves presented two alleged alien corpses and videos of Mexican pilots' encounters with fast-moving flying objects.
Ryan Graves lamented the display took away from pilots' UAP experiences and called Maussan's presentation an 'unsubstantiated stunt.'
Scientists have previously discredited alleged alien corpses Maussan presented as evidence of alien life.
Experts asked legislators to recognize UAP, guarantee airspace security, and allow UAP to be studied.
novelty_signals: Legislative effort to formally acknowledge alien life at the national level
Presentation of alleged alien corpses to a national congress
Cross-national witness testimony with former U.S. Navy pilot testifying before Mexican Congress
Proposed law would be first in the world to formally acknowledge presence of alien life on Earth
parsed.summary: A September 2003 U.S. Embassy Mexico cable reports on Mexican Congressional testimony regarding UAP, where experts including journalist Jaime Maussan and former U.S. Navy pilot Ryan Graves presented alleged alien corpses and pilot encounter videos as part of debate on the Aerial Space Protection Law. Graves subsequently distanced himself from Maussan's presentation, calling it an 'unsubstantiated stunt,' and scientists had previously discredited similar claims by Maussan.

title: DOW-UAP-D12, Mission Report, Iraq, May 2022

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed one UAP at 2043Z on 20 May 2022 flying north to northeast from grid 38SMC79xx70xx while the friendly aircraft was at 18,000 feet near grid 38SMC85xx77xx in Iraq.
The screener followed the UAP as long as possible but could not achieve a positive identification.
The observing asset was conducting a reconnaissance mission under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE, collecting SIGINT and providing ISR support to OP PHANTOM FLEX for approximately 18 hours.
The UAP's altitude, depth, velocity, trajectory, and physical state were all reported as unknown.
The document was originally classified SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY and declassified on 8 October 2025 by MG Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff.
novelty_signals: The observing platform was a SIGINT/FMV reconnaissance asset with an 18-hour mission duration, suggesting a remotely piloted aircraft (likely MQ-9) rather than a manned fighter, which is an uncommon observer type in UAP reports.
Despite having FMV capability and ANDAS4 targeting pod on station, the screener could not positively identify the object.
All kinematic parameters of the UAP (altitude, velocity, trajectory) were reported as unknown, indicating the sensors could not characterize the object's flight characteristics.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force reconnaissance asset operating under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE in Iraq on 20 May 2022 observed a single UAP at 2043Z flying north to northeast, which the crew followed as long as possible but could not positively identify. The mission report, originally classified SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY, was declassified on 8 October 2025 and lists all UAP kinematic parameters as unknown despite the aircraft carrying FMV and SIGINT collection systems.

title: DOW-UAP-D19, Mission Report, Syria, February 21, 2023

key_claims: A 2-ship of F-15E aircraft observed 3 possible UAP at FL240 (approximately 24,000 feet) in the vicinity of Shaddadi, Syria, with weapon system video produced but no further action taken.
The same flight observed 1 possible balloon at FL210 (approximately 21,000 feet) also near Shaddadi approximately 70 minutes after the initial UAP sighting.
The UAP produced no radar returns on the APG-82 radar; 2 of the 3 objects were described as white objects with infrared significance.
The flight experienced 3 minutes of MFT radar jamming in the X-band (8.8-9.9 GHz) near Shaddadi, assessed as likely originating from a Turkish X-band jammer on or near the Syria-Turkey border.
No health effects were experienced by aircrew during the UAP encounter.
novelty_signals: Three UAP observed visually and on IR but with zero radar returns despite an APG-82 AESA radar operating in X-band — suggesting low radar cross-section objects.

UAP sighting occurred within minutes of confirmed electronic warfare activity (radar jamming) in the same geographic area, raising the question of correlation between EW environment and UAP observations.
The document explicitly notes the objects were 'IR significant' (detectable in infrared) despite being invisible to radar, indicating a thermal signature without a corresponding radar signature.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force F-15E flight conducting defensive counter-air operations over Syria on 21 February 2023 observed three possible UAP at FL240 and one possible balloon at FL210 near Shaddadi, producing weapon system video but taking no further action. The UAP were IR-significant white objects with no radar returns, observed shortly after the flight experienced X-band radar jamming assessed as likely originating from a Turkish jammer near the Syria-Turkey border.

title: DOW-UAP-D20, Mission Report, Iraq, 2023

key_claims: A 2-ship of F-16CM observed 10-20 possible UAP maneuvering quickly west to east northeast of the Recognized Land Zone at FL600+ altitude on 31 March 2023.
The flight obtained a track on a possible UAP via the SNIPER targeting pod in TV mode for approximately 20 seconds before the object dimmed and disappeared from the pod.
Analyst comparison of targeting pod imagery between the possible UAP and a star showed different results, suggesting the objects were not stars.
None of the objects were seen in any formations as previously seen in prior sorties, indicating recurring UAP encounters in the same operational area.
No RF signatures, effects on persons, or recognizable UAP physical state were reported.
novelty_signals: Reference to prior sorties with UAP in formations implies a pattern of recurring encounters in the Iraq/Syria theater.
Deliberate analyst comparison of targeting pod signatures between UAP and a known star, with differing results, constitutes a basic sensor-discrimination test.
Estimated altitude FL600+ (above 60,000 feet) places the objects well above the F-16 operational ceiling.
Objects tracked on SNIPER targeting pod in TV mode dimmed and disappeared after ~20 seconds, suggesting active luminosity change rather than simple loss of track.
parsed.summary: A 2-ship F-16CM flight conducting defensive counter-air operations over Iraq/Syria on 31 March 2023 observed 10-20 bright objects maneuvering quickly at FL600+ altitude, tracking one on a SNIPER targeting pod for approximately 20 seconds before it dimmed and vanished. An analyst comparison of the targeting pod imagery between a possible UAP and a star yielded different results, and the crew noted the objects were not in formations seen during prior sorties.

title: DOW-UAP-D25, Mission Report, Greece, January 2024

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed one UAP traveling at approximately 434 knots while in transit over the eastern Mediterranean on 25 January 2024.
The UAP was diamond-shaped with a non-maneuvering probe at the bottom and was only visible on the SWIR (Short-Wave Infrared) camera, not other sensors.
The UAP maintained a steady flight path, increased and decreased altitude profile, but did not change trajectory, and was assessed as benign.
The observation lasted approximately 2 minutes (0509Z to 0511Z) at an estimated altitude of FL200, with the friendly aircraft at FL250.
The observer assessed the UAP propulsion means as unknown, and no RF emissions, advanced materials, effects on equipment, or effects on persons were reported.
novelty_signals: UAP visible only on SWIR sensor — invisible to other onboard systems, suggesting selective spectral signature
Precise speed estimate of 434 knots for a UAP assessed as having unknown propulsion
Diamond shape with non-maneuvering tail/probe is an uncommon morphology in UAP reporting
UAP maintained controlled flight — steady path with altitude variation but no trajectory change — suggesting intelligent control despite UNK assessment
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircraft operating out of LGLR (Greece) on 25 January 2024 observed a diamond-shaped UAP with a non-maneuvering probe, traveling at approximately 434 knots at FL200, visible only on the SWIR camera for roughly two minutes before it departed without incident. The observer assessed the UAP as benign with unknown propulsion, and no anomalous effects on personnel or equipment were reported.

title: DOW-UAP-D27, Mission Report, United Arab Emirates, October 2023

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed one UAP during return to base at 0457Z on 7 June 2024, described as a glowing hot spherical object with a vertical cylindrical pole/bar attached to its bottom and a possible reflection in the water below.
The UAP was observed flying straight just over the water at an estimated speed of 140 knots while the friendly aircraft was at 23,999 feet MSL traveling at 163 knots.
The UAP showed no response to observer actions, no advanced capabilities or materials, no RF emissions, and was assessed as benign by the observer.
The UAP's propulsion means was reported as unknown, its physical state was solid, and no objects or materials were recovered.
The mission was an ISR sortie under Operation ENDURING SENTINEL, with the primary tasking involving scanning for dhow activity near a surveillance point in the Gulf of Oman.
novelty_signals: Detailed morphology description of a glowing hot spherical object with an attached vertical cylindrical pole/bar appendage, an unusual UAP shape not commonly reported.
Possible reflection of the object visible in the water surface below, suggesting strong thermal or luminous emission.
Low-altitude high-speed transit just over water at 140 knots contrasts with the observing aircraft at nearly 24,000 feet, indicating significant altitude separation.
Object observed via FMV (full-motion video) sensor suite including AN/DAS-1 targeting pod, providing potential recorded imagery.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircraft operating under Operation ENDURING SENTINEL observed a single UAP during return to base over the Gulf of Oman on 7 June 2024, described as a glowing hot spherical object with a vertical cylindrical appendage flying just above the water at 140 knots. The observer assessed the UAP as benign with unknown propulsion, no advanced capabilities, and no reaction to the aircraft's presence.

title: DOW-UAP-D28, Mission Report, Iraq, September 2024

object_types: solid object with significant IR heat signature
key_claims: During a weapons calibration test involving an AGM-176 Griffin missile, a UAP flew through the aircraft sensor field of view at a high rate of speed between munition release and munition impact.
The UAP created an IR lens flare on both MX-20 and MX-25 sensors, indicating a significant heat source.
The UAP's path of movement appeared predetermined and not in response to the aircraft's detection.
It is unknown whether an object detached itself from the primary UAP immediately before leaving the sensor field of view.
No third-party observers reported an additional aircraft in the airspace, and the crew did not reobserve the UAP after the event.
novelty_signals: Dual-sensor IR corroboration: UAP simultaneously triggered lens flare on both MX-20 and MX-25 IR sensors, indicating a real thermal source rather than a single-sensor artefact.
Possible object separation: observers noted uncertainty about whether a secondary object detached from the primary UAP before it left the field of view.
UAP appeared during a live weapons employment (AGM-176 firing), transiting the sensor FOV between release and impact — an operationally sensitive window.
Observer assessment was 'Benign' despite the UAP being solid, fast-moving, unidentified, and unresponsive to observation, with no IFF interrogation conducted.
parsed.summary: A U.S. military aircraft conducting armed overwatch and weapons calibration over Iraq on 20 September 2024 observed a solid UAP transit its MX-20 and MX-25 IR sensor fields of view at high speed during an AGM-176 Griffin missile shot, producing significant IR lens flare indicating a substantial heat source. The UAP's movement appeared predetermined and unresponsive to detection, was not reacquired after the event, and a possible secondary object separation was noted but remains unconfirmed.

title: DOW-UAP-D3, Mission Report, Arabian Gulf, 2020

object_types: line of dots followed by a trailing dot
key_claims: At approximately 1736Z, 4 UAP were observed beneath the aircraft
1 UAP observed at 17:36:22, 2 UAP observed side by side at 17:36:30, and 1 UAP observed at 17:36:49
Cloud coverage obstructed the observer from following and getting a clear visual
UAP showed no advanced capabilities and/or materials
The UAP were described as a line of dots followed by a trailing dot
novelty_signals: Multiple UAP appearing in rapid sequence within 27 seconds suggests coordinated movement or a single phenomenon
Two UAP observed side by side at 17:36:30 implies formation-like behavior
ISR mission platform was actively tasked when UAP were encountered, not a chance sighting
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR mission operating under AFCENT in the Arabian Gulf in 2020 observed four UAP appearing in rapid succession over a 27-second window, described as a line of dots with a trailing dot. Cloud cover prevented sustained visual tracking, and the report explicitly notes no advanced capabilities or materials were observed.

title: DOW-UAP-D4, Mission Report, Arabian Gulf, 2020

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed a possible UAP at 1258Z at grid reference 34SDG9041417044
The UAP's velocity was estimated at 321 knots (369 mph)
The UAP increased speed and changed direction towards the east
Brief observation precluded altitude estimates of the UAP
The pilot's identity and additional details are redacted under (b)(6) privacy exemptions
novelty_signals: UAP demonstrated apparent acceleration and directional change, suggesting controlled or anomalous flight behavior
MGRS coordinate provided gives precise geolocation of the sighting
Observation was too brief to estimate altitude, suggesting high speed or sudden appearance
parsed.summary: A U.S. military operator in the Arabian Gulf in 2020 observed a possible UAP at grid reference 34SDG9041417044 traveling at an estimated 321 knots, which then increased speed and changed direction towards the east. The brief observation precluded altitude estimates, and the pilot's identity is redacted under privacy exemptions.

title: DOW-UAP-D42, Range Fouler Debrief, Japan, 2023

key_claims: Observer saw an initial object fly through the radar screen and began tracking it
A second object of same size and shape surpassed the first at much higher speed
Three UAP were observed on screen simultaneously moving amongst each other
The contact altitude was approximately 18000 feet
The event occurred at dusk during an ISR mission in the Arabian Gulf
novelty_signals: Multiple UAP operating in coordinated proximity, moving amongst each other
Second object matched first in size and shape but exhibited significantly higher speed
Objects detected on sensor screen during active ISR mission, not just visual sighting
Wind conditions noted as 150/230 suggesting objects were not wind-driven
parsed.summary: A U.S. military pilot from the 482nd Attack Squadron reported detecting three UAP on sensor during an ISR mission over the Arabian Gulf at dusk on 31 August 2020, with one object overtaking another of identical size and shape at much higher speed. All three objects were observed moving amongst each other simultaneously at approximately 18,000 feet altitude.

title: DOW-UAP-D44, Range Fouler Reporting Form, Gulf of Aden, October 2020

key_claims: A round, cold object was detected via IR sensor at 14:18:39Z on 15 October 2020 over the Gulf of Aden
The object was traveling at 319 degrees (northwest) at approximately 20 mph
The object made abrupt directional changes during the approximately 1-minute contact
The observer was at 19,073 feet HAT with the sensor aimed -50 degrees below altitude at a slant range of 4.06NM and ground range of 4.78KM
The IR sensor was set to black hot and the object appeared bright white, indicating it was cold relative to its surroundings
novelty_signals: Object described as cold in IR (bright white on black-hot polarity) despite being airborne, inconsistent with conventional powered aircraft
Abrupt directional changes at low speed (20 mph) suggest non-ballistic, non-conventional flight characteristics
Detection by 1172 ATKS (Attack Squadron) during ISR mission indicates military sensor-grade observation
parsed.summary: A U.S. military operator from the 1172 ATKS observed a round, cold object via infrared sensor over the Gulf of Aden on 15 October 2020, traveling northwest at approximately 20 mph at a slant range of 4.06 nautical miles. The object made abrupt directional changes during the roughly one-minute encounter and appeared anomalously cold on the IR sensor.

title: DOW-UAP-D48, Department of the Air Force Report, 1996

key_claims: Mode-5 failure responses, though rare, account for approximately 90% of total risks to people inside impact limit lines for Atlas IIA launches.
The Mode-5 impact density function uses two shaping constants (A and B) to model the probability of vehicle impacts at varying angular deviations and ranges from the flight line.
Historical launch failure data from Atlas, Delta, and Titan programs (1,186 flights total) were filtered to estimate failure probabilities and response-mode percentages.

Parts-analysis reliability approaches are fundamentally flawed for complex launch systems due to undetected design flaws, manufacturing variations, and invalid assumptions about component independence.
Simulation of vehicle malfunction turns (random-attitude and slow-turn failures) is necessary to determine optimum shaping constants because the historical Mode-5 failure sample is too small.
novelty_signals: This document is a space-booster risk analysis report with no UAP/UFO content despite being catalogued in the war.gov/UFO PURSUE collection
Detailed appendix contains complete launch and failure histories for Atlas, Delta, Titan, and Thor programs through August 1996
parsed.summary: This 1996 Research Triangle Institute report develops a methodology for modeling unlikely space-booster failure modes (Mode-5 responses) that cause vehicles to deviate significantly from their intended flight lines, using simulation-derived shaping constants for the DAMP risk-analysis program. It compiles comprehensive launch and failure histories for Atlas, Delta, Titan, and Thor vehicles and estimates failure probabilities and response-mode percentages from empirical data filtered across 1,186 launches.

title: DOW-UAP-D49, Launch Summary, Vandenberg AFB, 2000

organisations: Boeing and Michigan Aeronautical Research Center
key_claims: Vandenberg AFB conducted approximately 1,790 major launch operations between 16 December 1958 and 3 February 2000
AFSC was the dominant launch agency with 677 launches through 1978, followed by SAC with 526
Launch vehicles ranged from early Thor and Atlas ICBMs/IRBMs to Titan IV, Peacekeeper, Delta II, Pegasus, and Taurus by the late 1990s
The Pegasus program began with three captive inert flights in 1989-90 before transitioning to live flights from Edwards AFB and later staging from Vandenberg
The document serves as the official registry maintained by the 30th Space Wing History Office and was distributed to military commands, NASA, and defence contractors
novelty_signals: This is a launch operations catalogue rather than a UAP observation report — its inclusion in the war.gov/UFO PURSUE collection is itself anomalous and may indicate interest in correlating UAP sightings with known missile and satellite launch activity at Vandenberg
parsed.summary: This document is the official chronological registry of all major launch operations conducted from Vandenberg Air Force Base, California, from the first launch on 16 December 1958 through 3 February 2000, totalling approximately 1,790 launches. It catalogues each launch by date, vehicle type, launch facility, program, and responsible command, supplemented by annual summary matrices, a launch facility guide, and a glossary of acronyms.

title: DOW-UAP-D5, Mission Report, Arabian Gulf, 2020

key_claims: At 1354Z, a single UAP was observed at MGRS 34SCE7566990098 traveling at 40 knots at FL160 to FL170 with constant speed.
At 2243Z, two possible UAPs were observed at MGRS 35TQK1580995057 traveling at an estimated 278 knots.
The two UAPs increased speed and changed direction towards the south.
Multiple sections of the report are redacted under exemption 1.4(a) (classified military/intelligence information) and (b)(6) (personal privacy).
novelty_signals: Two distinct sightings reported in a single MISREP with markedly different velocities (40 knots vs 278 knots), suggesting either different object types or dramatic speed variation.
The second observation describes UAPs that both accelerated and changed heading, indicating apparent controlled maneuvering.
MGRS grid coordinates provided give precise geolocation for both encounters.
parsed.summary: A U.S. military Mission Report (MISREP) documents two separate UAP observations: one object at 40 knots holding constant speed at FL160-FL170, and two possible UAPs at 278 knots that accelerated and changed direction southward. Both sightings include precise MGRS grid references, with substantial redactions under national security and privacy exemptions.

title: DOW-UAP-D50, Email Correspondence, INDOPACOM, April 2025

organisations: Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security
key_claims: US aircraft observed 1 possible UAP for 12 seconds at 2353Z on 10 April 2025, flying at unknown altitude and speed with no interference noted.
US aircraft observed 1 possible UAP for 23 seconds at 0007Z on 11 April 2025, flying at unknown altitude and speed with no interference noted.
The tearline summaries of both sightings were confirmed approved at the UNCLASSIFIED level.
The area of responsibility (AOR) designation as INDOPACOM was also confirmed at the UNCLASSIFIED level.
The underlying mission report content is classified SECRET//NOFORN while only the tearline summaries are unclassified.
novelty_signals: Two UAP sightings occurred within 14 minutes of each other spanning midnight UTC, suggesting a possible recurring or persistent object.
Document reveals the bureaucratic process of declassifying UAP tearlines, showing how classification decisions are negotiated between units and disclosure analysts.
parsed.summary: This email correspondence documents two brief UAP sightings by US aircraft in the INDOPACOM area of responsibility on 10-11 April 2025, each lasting 12 and 23 seconds respectively at unknown altitude and speed with no interference. The emails concern confirming that the tearline summaries of these sightings from a classified mission report are approved for release at the UNCLASSIFIED level.

title: DOW-UAP-D51, Email Correspondence, Pacific Time Zone, March 2023

organisations: Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security
key_claims: A civilian reported observing a large blue featureless triangular object emitting powerful whitish blue light from multiple points along its perimeter near a national security facility at night in March 2023.
The object hovered stationary above or near a national security facility for approximately three minutes before moving in a jerking or jumping manner inconsistent with smooth jet propulsion.
The reporter could not discern how the object was controlled, its means of propulsion, or whether it had a defined front or rear, and stated they did not think it was a drone.
The original Intelligence Information Report (IIR) was classified SECRET//NOFORN and a derivative classification review was approved to use an unclassified summary in a product.
The object was observed for approximately eight minutes and did not appear to travel along a defined flight path or emit a vapor trail.
novelty_signals: Erratic jerking/jumping motion described as inconsistent with conventional jet propulsion
Object described as featureless with no discernible front, rear, or means of propulsion
Stationary hovering near a national security facility by a civilian witness
Derivative classification review process used instead of standard lengthy declassification, suggesting procedural novelty within the reporting chain
parsed.summary: This document consists of email correspondence between an AFOSI intelligence oversight official and a DoD information disclosure analyst regarding the derivative classification review of a SECRET//NOFORN Intelligence Information Report describing a civilian sighting of a large blue triangular UAP near a national security facility in the Pacific Time Zone in March 2023. The UAP was reported as featureless, emitting whitish blue light, hovering for three minutes, and then moving in erratic jerking motions inconsistent with conventional propulsion over an approximately eight-minute observation period.

title: DOW-UAP-D52, Email Correspondance, NA, August 2024

The document reveals an internal approval process for declassifying even basic temporal details like the year of an incident
parsed.summary: This email correspondence between a PAROC Intel Data Analysis Technician at 15 AF / DET 1 and an Information Disclosure Analyst discusses adding the year to an unclassified tear line describing a UAP sighting on 31 October 2024, in which a U.S. aircraft observed an oval/orb-shaped object at low speed for over two hours. The exchange reveals the deliberate review process governing what temporal details can be released in unclassified summaries of UAP mission reports.

title: DOW-UAP-D55, Mission Report, Syria, November 2016

key_claims: P-8A observed an unidentified low-flying object 86 nm northwest of Latakia traveling at approximately 500 knots on a southeasterly heading outbound from KCTG.
The object appeared to be in sea skim mode as detected via the EO/IR sensor.
P-8 lost visual of the object after approximately 2 minutes, at a point approximately 40 nm northwest of Latakia.
The object was observed to pass between the Russian vessel INGUL ARS and one unidentified vessel.
This was the first observed occurrence of possible missile activity by P-8 aircraft in the Eastern Mediterranean, assessed to be standard activity consistent with KCTG operations.
novelty_signals: Object characterized as possible missile but filed as UAP, suggesting identification remained uncertain
Sea skim mode at 500 knots is consistent with anti-ship cruise missile profile rather than typical UAP descriptions
First observed occurrence of this activity type by P-8 in the Eastern Mediterranean noted explicitly
parsed.summary: A U.S. Navy P-8A crew monitoring KCTG activity in the Eastern Mediterranean on 18 November 2016 detected an unidentified low-flying object via EO/IR sensor approximately 86 nm northwest of Latakia, Syria, traveling at roughly 500 knots in sea skim mode on a southeasterly heading. Visual contact was lost after two minutes near 40 nm northwest of Latakia, with the object passing between the Russian vessel INGUL ARS and an unidentified vessel.

title: DOW-UAP-D56, Range Fouler Debrief, Arabian Sea, August 2020

key_claims: A Navy O-3 pilot from HSM-73 observed 3 unidentified small air contacts during routine night operations in the North Arabian Sea on 2020-08-24 at 00:04:30Z
The contacts had no electronic support (ES), radar track, or IFF track and their distance, speed, and precise course were unknown
The pilot initially observed one unknown air contact, lost sight of it behind a cloud, and upon regaining contact found two additional contacts due east of the first
All three unknown air contacts appeared to maintain their relative course, speed, and altitude throughout the observation
The contacts were described as having wings/airframe structure and appeared to be on a westerly heading at approximately 22,000 feet altitude with wind direction 310 degrees
novelty_signals: Group of three UAP maintaining consistent relative formation (course, speed, altitude) suggests coordinated behavior
Objects appeared and multiplied from one to three during brief loss of visual contact behind a cloud
No sensor detection despite radar-equipped platform: negative ES, radar track, and IFF track on all three contacts
Night observation at approximately 22,000 feet altitude with round shape and wings/airframe morphology checked on the form
parsed.summary: A U.S. Navy O-3 pilot from HSM-73 filed a Range Fouler Debrief reporting three unidentified small air contacts observed during routine night operations over the North Arabian Sea on 24 August 2020, describing objects with wings/airframe structure on a westerly heading at approximately 22,000 feet that produced no electronic, radar, or IFF signatures. The pilot initially tracked one contact, lost it behind a cloud, then regained contact and observed two additional objects due east of the first, with all three maintaining consistent relative course, speed, and altitude.

title: DOW-UAP-D57, Range Fouler Reporting Form, Gulf of Aden, September 2020

key_claims: A round, cold object was tracked via IR sensor over the Gulf of Aden for 8 minutes from 21:09z to 21:17z on 04 September 2020.
The object was traveling 168 degrees at 277 mph and made a few abrupt directional changes during the encounter.
The sensor was aimed -39 degrees below aircraft altitude with a slant range of 6.1 NM and ground range of 8.81 KM, at an aircraft altitude of 23,819 feet HAT.
The object appeared bright white on a black-hot IR setting, indicating it was thermally cold relative to the background.
One contact was reported in the group with no radar trackfile, no ECM indications, and no visible wings, airframe, or propulsion.
novelty_signals: Object appeared cold (bright white in black-hot IR polarity), suggesting no conventional thermal signature from propulsion or friction heating at 277 mph.
Abrupt directional changes at 277 mph with no apparent propulsion system observed.
Standardised Range Fouler Reporting Form indicates an institutionalised Navy process for UAP encounters during active operations.
Object tracked at relatively close range (6.1 NM slant, 8.81 KM ground) for an extended 8-minute window.
parsed.summary: A U.S. military ISR operator flying at 23,819 feet over the Gulf of Aden on 4 September 2020 tracked a round, thermally cold object for eight minutes using an IR sensor, observing it travel at 277 mph on a 168-degree heading with abrupt directional changes. The object displayed no visible propulsion, wings, or airframe, and appeared bright white against a black-hot IR background, indicating anomalous thermal characteristics.

title: DOW-UAP-D58, Range Fouler Debrief, NA, October 2020

key_claims: Two UAP contacts were detected at 26,000 feet altitude, described as balloon-shaped, metallic, and reflective with red blinking strobes.
One range fouler was circling around the other, and both disappeared within 1/30th of a second.
Noise jamming was received during the encounter, indicated by two chevrons on the radar display.
The operator was unable to close within 16.9 nautical miles of the contacts despite obtaining radar lock and target pod video.
The contacts produced two IR-significant signatures on the target pod.
novelty_signals: Disappearance of both objects within 1/30th of a second suggests anomalous kinematics or sensor spoofing.
Active noise jamming received from the UAP, indicated by electronic countermeasure chevrons — suggests electronic warfare capability.
One object circling the other implies coordinated behavior between the two UAP.
Inability to close within 16.9 NM despite radar lock suggests the objects maintained standoff distance or exhibited evasive maneuvering.
parsed.summary: A U.S. military operator reported a nighttime encounter on 27 October 2020 with two balloon-shaped, metallic, reflective UAP at 26,000 feet that exhibited red blinking strobes, with one circling the other before both vanished in 1/30th of a second. The encounter included electronic countermeasures in the form of noise jamming, and the operator was unable to close within 16.9 NM despite achieving radar lock and target pod video.

title: DOW-UAP-D61, Mission Report, Arabian Gulf, August 2020

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed a formation of unknown flying objects traveling NE-NW along the coast in the Arabian Gulf at 1527Z on 27 August 2020.
The formation was tracked for approximately 2 minutes before positive identification was lost in cloud cover, and the aircrew was unable to regain PID.
Light cloud coverage prevented the continuous tracking of the UAP event.
The observing aircraft received a guard call from Iranian Air Defense at 0532Z, which was described as professional in tone with no mission impacts.
The mission was a 21-hour armed reconnaissance (AREC) flight collecting SIGINT and IMINT in support of NAVCENT operations in the Arabian Gulf region.
novelty_signals: Formation-level UAP sighting: multiple objects flying in coordinated formation rather than a single object.
Weather explicitly cited as preventing continuous tracking of the UAP event, noted in a dedicated WEATHER field tied to the observation.
Observation occurred during an active ISR mission with sensor suite (ANDAS4, AH_GMESH) yet the formation still could not be re-acquired after cloud obscuration.
Proximity to Iranian military airspace and concurrent Iranian Air Defense guard call adds geopolitical context uncommon in UAP reports.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force 482 ATKS crew conducting armed reconnaissance over the Arabian Gulf on 27 August 2020 observed a formation of unknown flying objects traveling northeast-to-northwest along the coast for approximately two minutes before losing track in cloud cover. The standardized MISREP, declassified on 22 January 2026 by USCENTCOM, documents the sighting alongside routine ISR activity, an Iranian Air Defense guard call, and vessel observations near Greater Tunb and Abu Musa Island.

title: DOW-UAP-D62, Mission Report, Strait of Hormuz, September 2020

key_claims: A U.S. Air Force asset observed a UAP at grid 39RVM5 at 1732Z on 16 September 2020, detected via FMV sensor, while operating at FL180 at 90 KIAS.
The aircraft experienced two separate lost-link events of unknown EMI type (11 minutes and 27 minutes), both causing complete system impact, flight path deviation, and medium mission impact.
Iranian Air Defense hailed the aircraft on guard frequency three times during the mission; standard responses were given with no impact to mission.

The aircraft was operating in support of NAVCENT to characterize Iranian/IRGCN vessels, UAS activity, port activity, and establish pattern of life in the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman.
An IR-class launcher was observed on Abu Musa Island and two possible Houdong-class vessels were observed docked pierside during the mission.
novelty_signals: Two EMI-induced complete lost-link events of unknown origin occurred in the same mission that also produced a UAP observation, suggesting possible correlation between electronic interference and UAP presence.
UAP was observed via FMV (full-motion video) from a remotely piloted aircraft, making this a sensor-detected rather than pilot-witnessed encounter.
The UAP observation occurred in an active military surveillance zone near Iranian territorial waters during an intelligence collection mission, placing it in a contested airspace context.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR asset operating from OKAS in support of NAVCENT observed a UAP via FMV at grid 39RVM5 in the Strait of Hormuz region at 1732Z on 16 September 2020, during a 20.9-hour reconnaissance mission that also involved three Iranian Air Defense guard calls and two unexplained EMI-induced lost-link events. The mission was declassified on 22 January 2026 by MG Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff.

title: DOW-UAP-D64, Mission Report, Iran, November 2020

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed two UAP on November 2, 2020, at 2143Z and 2148Z, during an armed reconnaissance mission over the Arabian Gulf region.
The first UAP was observed at an unknown altitude with a bearing of 080 T near grid 39RWK; the second UAP was observed five minutes later traveling northwest.
Both UAP were detected via FMV (Full Motion Video) and the footage was exploited by DOSI.
The aircraft was hailed on guard frequency by Iranian Air Defense during the mission at 1012Z; the interaction was professional with no impact to the mission.
Haze precluded IMINT collection effectiveness, and no UUV was identified during open water scans.
novelty_signals: Two UAP observed within a five-minute window in the same grid square area, suggesting either two distinct objects or rapid repositioning of a single object.
Observation occurred during an active ISR mission near Iranian airspace with concurrent Iranian air defense interaction, placing the sighting in a contested operational environment.
FMV sensor captured the UAP, meaning video evidence exists and was formally exploited by DOSI.
parsed.summary: This is a U.S. Air Force mission report (MISREP) from the 482nd Attack Squadron documenting an armed reconnaissance flight on November 2-3, 2020, during which the crew observed two unidentified aerial phenomena near grid 39RWK in the Arabian Gulf region at 2143Z and 2148Z via full motion video. The first UAP was at unknown altitude on bearing 080 T, while the second was observed traveling northwest five minutes later; the aircraft was operating at FL220 and had also been hailed by Iranian Air Defense earlier in the mission.

title: DOW-UAP-D7, Mission Report, Arabian Gulf, 2020

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed a UAP described as looking like a balloon, similar to previously reported UAP from 48FW.
The UAP was traveling with the winds at approximately 31,000 ft MSL.
A weapons quality 1 track was obtained on the UAP.
The operator was able to make a next to shoot determination on the track and visually identified the UAP via TFLIR.
The incident occurred in the vicinity of coordinates referenced as 323'S in the Arabian Gulf.
novelty_signals: Weapons quality track obtained on a balloon-like UAP at 31,000 ft, indicating it was treated as a potential threat
Next to shoot determination was made, suggesting rules of engagement were actively considered
Reference to similar previously reported UAP from 48FW indicates a pattern of recurring sightings
parsed.summary: A U.S. military mission report from the Arabian Gulf in 2020 documents the observation of a balloon-like UAP traveling with the winds at 31,000 ft MSL, tracked via infrared sensor (TFLIR) with a weapons quality 1 track. The operator obtained a next to shoot determination and visually identified the object, noting its similarity to previously reported UAP from the 48th Fighter Wing.

title: DOW-UAP-D74, Mission Report, Syria, November 2023

key_claims: A U.S. military operator observed one UAP shaped as a bouncy ball while returning to base at 2153Z on 9 November 2023 in Syria.
The UAP traveled at approximately 424 knots (483 mph) consistently for at least 7 minutes, approaching from the south at near co-altitude before dropping altitude and safely passing the aircraft.
No emissions were detected from the UAP, it was assessed as benign, and it had no effects on the aircrew or equipment.
The UAP's propulsion means was unknown, it appeared solid, and it was assessed as not under intelligent control.
The UAP was reported to exhibit advanced capabilities: sustained ~424 knot speed for at least 7 minutes in the shape of a bouncy ball.
novelty_signals: Spherical 'bouncy ball' morphology is uncommon in UAP reporting.
Sustained high speed (~424 knots) for 7+ minutes with no detectable emissions or propulsion.
UAP dropped altitude and safely passed the aircraft, suggesting possible awareness of the observer despite being assessed as not under intelligent control.
Observer explicitly noted advanced capabilities despite assessing the object as benign.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR asset operating over Syria on 9 November 2023 observed a solid, bouncy-ball-shaped UAP approaching from the south at near co-altitude, traveling consistently at approximately 424 knots for at least 7 minutes before passing safely and moving out of range. The object emitted no signals, was assessed as benign and not under intelligent control, though the reporter flagged its sustained speed and shape as advanced capabilities.

title: DOW-UAP-D75, Mission Report, Gulf of Aden, July 2024

key_claims: A U.S. Air Force operator observed 1 UAP on 14 July 2024 at 0517Z in the Gulf of Aden region at MGRS 38P MT 53 17, which maintained a straight flight path at the same altitude.
The UAP's speed was faster than the observing aircraft's flying speed, and the operator followed it until the distance became too far to follow.
The observer assessed the UAP as benign, with no effects on persons or equipment, no engagement, and no material recovered.
The UAP's propulsion means, whether it was under intelligent control, and its advanced capabilities were all reported as unknown.
The UAP traveled on a northwest trajectory at low altitude from MGRS 38P MT 53 17 to 38P MT 22 49, with all kinetic measurements estimated rather than measured.
novelty_signals: UAP speed exceeded the military aircraft's own flying speed, implying performance beyond the observer platform's capability.
Observer attempted to follow the UAP but was unable to keep pace, suggesting significant velocity differential.
Observer rank identified as TSgt/E-5, an enlisted sensor operator rather than a pilot, indicating this was likely a remotely piloted aircraft (drone) crew observation.
Unit 124 ATKS (Attack Squadron) and mission profile suggest an MQ-9 Reaper or similar RPA platform was the observer asset.
parsed.summary: A USCENTCOM mission report from 14 July 2024 documents a U.S. Air Force 124th Attack Squadron crew observing a single UAP during an ISR mission in the Gulf of Aden that flew a straight northwest path at low altitude faster than the military aircraft could follow. The observer assessed the object as benign with unknown propulsion and no anomalous effects on personnel or equipment, and all kinetic parameters were estimated rather than instrumentally measured.

title: DOW-UAP-D8, Mission Report, Djibouti, 2025

classifications: REL TO USA, FIN, SWE, FVEY, NATO
key_claims: At 1653Z, an observer detected 2 round white hot UAPs moving dynamically south at approximately 240 nautical miles per hour.
The UAPs were observed in the vicinity of MGRS grid 35SQT3423692957, placing them over the Mediterranean Sea.
The report was classified SECRET and releasable to USA, Finland, Sweden, Five Eyes, and NATO partners.
Multiple sections of the mission report were redacted under exemption 1.4(a), indicating classified national security information.
novelty_signals: Unusual releasability markings including Finland and Sweden specifically, suggesting a NATO-adjacent multinational intelligence sharing context.
Two UAPs observed simultaneously moving in coordinated southward direction.
Speed estimate of 240 knots is within conventional aircraft range, not anomalous in itself.
parsed.summary: A U.S. military mission report from Djibouti documents the observation at 1653Z of two round, white-hot UAPs traveling south at approximately 240 knots near MGRS grid 35SQT3423692957 in the Mediterranean Sea. The report is heavily redacted under exemption 1.4(a) and was classified SECRET with broad NATO and partner-nation releasability.

title: DOW-UAP-PR19, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, May 2022

key_claims: A U.S. military aircraft observed 5 UAPs between 1514Z and 1934Z on 6 May 2022 in the Middle East during Operation INHERENT RESOLVE.
The first UAP had the visual appearance of a possible missile flying across the sensor field of view.
The remaining four UAPs fit closer to the profile of possible birds.
Dust conditions hindered most full-motion video collection of the ground.
Full motion video was exploited by DGS1 and the observation was made via infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform.
novelty_signals: Mixed identification within a single sighting event: one object assessed as possible missile morphology while four others assessed as possible birds, suggesting heterogeneous UAP reporting.
Extremely brief video evidence — only five seconds of footage for the entire observation window spanning over four hours.
Degraded sensor conditions due to dust noted, reducing confidence in visual identification.
parsed.summary: A U.S. military aircraft operating under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE in the Middle East on 6 May 2022 observed five unidentified anomalous phenomena over a period of approximately four hours, with the first resembling a possible missile and the remaining four fitting the profile of possible birds. The report, originally classified SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY, was declassified on 7 October 2025 by MG Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff.

title: DOW-UAP-PR20, Unresolved UAP Report, Kuwait, May 2022

organisations: Office of Prepublication and Security Review
key_claims: USCENTCOM submitted a UAP report to AARO consisting of a still image derived from a U.S. military system in 2022.
The original reporter digitally altered the imagery by adding a red line encircling an area of interest before submitting it to AARO.
An accompanying mission report, DoW-UAP-D12, described the UAP as moving from north to northeast.
The operator reported that they were unable to positively identify the UAP.
The image contains an encircled, elongated area of contrast that increases in intensity along its length from top left to bottom right.
novelty_signals: Original reporter digitally altered the imagery before submission, raising chain-of-custody concerns.
UAP described as moving from north to northeast, suggesting directional tracking was performed.
parsed.summary: USCENTCOM submitted to AARO an unresolved UAP report from 2022 consisting of a digitally annotated still image captured by a U.S. military system, depicting an elongated area of contrast that the operator was unable to identify. The original reporter altered the image by adding a red encirclement before submission, and an accompanying mission report described the object as moving from north to northeast.

title: DOW-UAP-PR21, Unresolved UAP Report, Iraq, May 2022

key_claims: A single small UAP was observed at 0117Z on 30 May 2022 flying north to northeast; the screener could not achieve a positive identification.
The accompanying mission report DoW-UAP-D14 described the UAP as a probable SU-27/35, suggesting a conventional aircraft identification.

The US military platform was reacted to by 1-3 aircraft including a possible Russian Air Force SU-30, which flew directly under its orbit at FL190 for approximately 2 minutes with no impact to the mission.

The mission conducted extensive ISR collection across 39 targets in the Israel-Lebanon-Syria region, observing Russian naval vessels including a Slava-class cruiser, Gorshkov-class frigate, and Udaloy I-class destroyer.
Video evidence consists of only ten seconds of infrared footage depicting two areas of contrast moving together near the center of the field of view.
novelty_signals: The UAP was observed in an operationally dense environment with confirmed Russian military air and naval activity, complicating attribution.
AARO's own comment and the mission report both suggest the UAP was likely a conventional SU-27/35 fighter aircraft, making this a candidate resolved case rather than a true anomaly.
The extremely short video duration (10 seconds) limits independent analytical value.
parsed.summary: A US military ISR platform operating over the Eastern Mediterranean in May 2022 observed a single UAP flying north to northeast that could not be positively identified by the screener, though the accompanying mission report assessed it as a probable SU-27/35 fighter. The mission also documented extensive Russian military activity including fighter aircraft operations at Bassel Al Assad airfield and multiple Russian naval vessels transiting the area.

title: DOW-UAP-PR22, Unresolved UAP Report, Syria, July 2022

key_claims: At 310239ZJUL22, a US military asset observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon in the vicinity of grid 37SFU271 in kill package 9 during Operation INHERENT RESOLVE in Syria.
The UAP event lasted less than one minute, with the object moving from north to south.
The observation was made from a single US military aircraft at 19,359 feet altitude traveling at 116 knots, with 14 seconds of video captured on both infrared and electro-optical sensors.
No UAP signatures (RF or other) were detected and no effects on personnel were reported.
The mission was a planned armed reconnaissance tasking by the 89th Attack Squadron supporting TF CHOSIN, operating from Muwaffaq Salti Air Base (OJMS) in Jordan.
novelty_signals: Dual-sensor capture (infrared and electro-optical simultaneously) provides potential for cross-sensor corroboration.
Very short duration event (less than one minute, 14 seconds of video) limits analytical depth but suggests rapid transient object.
UAP observed during an active armed reconnaissance mission in an active combat zone (Syria), which is atypical compared to training-range sightings.
No UAP physical state, altitude, depth, velocity, or trajectory data was recorded despite dual-sensor availability — all fields left blank.
parsed.summary: A US military aircraft conducting armed reconnaissance over Syria on 30-31 July 2022 in support of Operation INHERENT RESOLVE observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon near grid 37SFU271 that moved from north to south in under one minute. The 14-second observation was captured on both infrared and electro-optical sensors, but no RF signatures, effects on personnel, or measurable flight characteristics of the object were recorded.

title: DOW-UAP-PR23, Unresolved UAP Report, Iraq, December 2022

key_claims: At 1620Z on 1 December 2022, a US military platform observed 1x possible UAP/UAV flying west to east in the vicinity of Baghdad, Iraq
The observation was captured in approximately ten seconds of infrared video footage
The observing aircraft did not follow the UAP and continued its ISR mission as tasked with no further events observed
The friendly aircraft was at FL180 altitude at the time of the UAP observation
The document was declassified by MG Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff, on 8 October 2025
novelty_signals: UAP observed during an active ISR mission supporting Operation INHERENT RESOLVE, not a dedicated UAP search
Crew elected not to pursue or further investigate the UAP, suggesting low perceived threat or priority
Sensor named AH/BLASPHEMY listed as available but no indication it was used to characterize the UAP
No UAP signatures, RF emissions, or effects on persons reported despite infrared detection
parsed.summary: A US military ISR platform conducting a SIGINT and surveillance mission over Baghdad, Iraq on 1 December 2022 observed a single possible UAP/UAV flying west to east, captured in approximately ten seconds of infrared video. The crew did not pursue the object and continued their mission; no anomalous signatures, RF emissions, or effects on personnel were reported.

title: DOW-UAP-PR27, Unresolved UAP Report, United Arab Emirates, October 2023

key_claims: Two separate UAP incidents were observed by a U.S. military aircraft operating from Al Dhafra (OMAM) on 24 October 2023: the first at 0241Z at grid 39RXK6 and the second at 0322Z at the same vicinity.
Both UAPs were assessed as benign, solid physical objects not under intelligent control, with no effects on persons or engagement by the observer.
The first UAP showed a thermal signature described as cold on IR, with an estimated velocity of 320 MPH; the second had an estimated velocity of 440 MPH with unknown signatures.

The aircraft received a professional guard call from Iranian Air Defense at 0145Z stating 'maintain safe distance from border', to which the crew responded they were conducting routine operations in international airspace.
The mission was a 20-hour 43-minute ISR sortie by the 50th Attack Squadron conducting IMINT in support of NAVCENT under Operation Spartan Shield.
novelty_signals: Two distinct UAP sightings on the same sortie separated by 41 minutes, with significantly different estimated velocities (320 vs 440 MPH), suggesting either two different objects or rapid acceleration.
UAP thermal signature described as cold on infrared, which is atypical for conventional aircraft or drones.
Proximity to Iranian airspace and concurrent Iranian Air Defense guard call raises the question of whether the UAPs were related to Iranian military activity.
The 4:57 IR video footage constitutes sensor-recorded evidence beyond witness testimony alone.
parsed.summary: A declassified USCENTCOM mission report documents two UAP incidents observed by a 50th Attack Squadron aircraft during a 20-hour ISR mission from Al Dhafra, UAE, on 24 October 2023, describing solid objects with cold thermal signatures at estimated speeds of 320 and 440 MPH, both assessed as benign and not under intelligent control. The sortie also involved a professional guard call from Iranian Air Defense and was accompanied by 4 minutes 57 seconds of infrared video footage submitted to AARO.

title: DOW-UAP-PR33, Unresolved UAP Report, Syria, October 2024

key_claims: At 1559Z on 20 October 2024, a US military platform observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon described as a misshapen and uneven ball of white light during an ISR mission over Syria.

Multiple glares or lights from unknown origin were observed at different angles and directions between 1559Z and 1644Z, with light/glare crossing directly on the FMV camera at 1559Z, 1602Z, and 1644Z.
A light/glare halo effect was observed at the top of the FMV feed at 1609Z and 1620Z.
The UAP physical state was classified as plasma, with unknown propulsion means, and the aircrew assessed the UAP as benign with no mission impact.
The aircrew assessed the phenomenon was not a lasing event.
novelty_signals: UAP physical state explicitly categorised as 'Plasma' in the structured report fields
Multiple distinct UAP manifestations over a 45-minute window (1559Z-1644Z) including both direct camera crossings and halo effects at different times
Aircrew specifically ruled out a lasing event, implying the light source was considered potentially hostile before being assessed as benign
Video evidence is only 5 seconds despite a 45-minute observation window, suggesting most footage remains classified or was not captured
parsed.summary: A US military ISR platform operating over Syria on 20 October 2024 during Operation INHERENT RESOLVE observed a UAP described as a misshapen and uneven ball of white light, classified as plasma, which produced multiple glares and a halo effect on its FMV camera feed over a 45-minute period. The aircrew assessed the phenomenon as benign with no mission impact, ruling out a lasing event, and the UAP showed no response to observation, no intelligent control, and no advanced capabilities.

title: DOW-UAP-PR34, Unresolved UAP Report, Greece, October 2023

key_claims: A UAP was observed flying just above the surface of the ocean water near Greece on 27 October 2023 at 0035Z.
The UAP made multiple 90-degree turns at an estimated speed of 80 MPH.
The UAP appeared seemingly circular but too small to make out details.
The UAP was tracked for approximately three minutes (0035Z to 0038Z) before being lost from the sensor feed.
The observer assessed the UAP as benign, with no intelligent control, no signatures, no effects on equipment or persons, and unknown propulsion means.
novelty_signals: Sharp 90-degree turns at 80 MPH near ocean surface — inconsistent with conventional fixed-wing or rotary-wing flight dynamics at that speed.
UAP assessed as solid physical object with unknown propulsion yet no RF signatures detected.
Very short observation window (under 3 minutes) before object was lost from an ISR platform specifically designed for persistent tracking.
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR platform operating under USCENTCOM observed a small, seemingly circular UAP flying just above the ocean surface near Greece on 27 October 2023, which executed multiple 90-degree turns at approximately 80 MPH before being lost from the sensor feed after roughly three minutes. The declassified mission report (MISREP 9329374) documents the UAP as a solid object with unknown propulsion and no detectable signatures, assessed as benign and not under intelligent control.

title: DOW-UAP-PR35, Unresolved UAP Report, Greece, October 2023

key_claims: A U.S. military platform operating under USCENTCOM observed a single UAP near Greece on 29 October 2023 at 0811Z, captured in 24 seconds of infrared video.
The UAP was described as seemingly circular, too small to make out details, flying just above the surface of the ocean toward land at an estimated 30 MPH.
The observer assessed the UAP as benign, with no anomalous signatures, no response to observer actions, no advanced capabilities confirmed, and no intelligent control detected.
The UAP was tracked by sensor until the background transitioned from water to land, at which point it became indistinguishable and was lost from the feed.
The UAP's physical state was assessed as solid, propulsion means unknown, and no material was recovered.
novelty_signals: UAP observed skimming just above the ocean surface, an uncommon flight profile distinct from typical high-altitude sightings
Object lost not due to speed or maneuver but because it became indistinguishable against a land background, suggesting low contrast or small thermal signature
Explicit assessment of 'NO' intelligent control and 'Benign' threat level recorded in structured military reporting format, which is relatively rare in released UAP documents
parsed.summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR platform operating under USCENTCOM observed a small, circular UAP flying just above the ocean surface near Greece on 29 October 2023, captured in 24 seconds of infrared video before the object became indistinguishable against a land background. The observer assessed the UAP as benign and solid with unknown propulsion, estimating its speed at 30 MPH, with no anomalous signatures, advanced capabilities, or intelligent control detected.

title: DOW-UAP-PR36, Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, May 2020

key_claims: A solid white round object was observed making erratic movements above the water during an ISR tasking on 14 May 2020 at 20:40Z.
The sensor operator continuously manipulated the sensor to maintain visual contact, as evidenced by intermittent visibility of water waves in the background.
The object produced an intermittent radar trackfile with one contact in the group and no electronic attack indications were noted.
The crew obtained 4x zoom on the object but lost it due to poor track placement.
The accompanying video footage is two minutes and 17 seconds from an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform.
novelty_signals: Erratic movement pattern above water surface observed on infrared
Object described as round and solid white in black-hot polarity, suggesting it was cooler or differently emissive than surroundings
Intermittent radar trackfile indicates the object was inconsistently detectable by radar
Sensor operator struggled to maintain track despite active manipulation, suggesting unusual movement characteristics
parsed.summary: A U.S. Central Command crew conducting an ISR mission in the Middle East on 14 May 2020 observed and recorded a solid white round object making erratic movements above the water, capturing two minutes and 17 seconds of infrared video before losing track due to poor track placement. The object produced an intermittent radar return with no electronic warfare indications and was reported to AARO via a Range Fouler Debrief Form, later declassified by MG Richard A. Harrison.

title: Western US Event

key_claims: Three teams of two federal law enforcement special agents independently observed orange orbs emitting or launching smaller red orbs in groups of two to four, occurring at least five times over two days at dusk.

AARO measurements assessed a stationary glowing orange orb to have been approximately 1050 meters from observers and between 12-18 meters in diameter, contradicting witness estimates of 500-600 meters and small helicopter cockpit size.
A pursued object initially mistaken for a car moved laterally off-road over desert terrain at 15-20 mph with zero apparent resistance and without changing orientation relative to observers.

A kite-shaped object observed through night vision goggles appeared somewhat transparent, with stars faintly visible through it, and a spotlight beam appeared to stop short when aimed at an area where the object had been.
In later discussions with AARO, the dark kite object was described as being triangular.
novelty_signals: Multiple independent witness teams of federal law enforcement agents corroborating the same phenomena from different vantage points
Object described as transparent or translucent with stars visible through it via NVGs
Orbs launching smaller orbs in a repeatable sequential pattern observed at least five times
Object pursued on a road moved laterally over desert terrain with zero apparent resistance
Spotlight beam appeared to be physically blocked by an invisible or near-invisible object
AARO provided post-hoc measurements that significantly revised witness distance and size estimates
parsed.summary: Seven federal law enforcement special agents reported four categories of unidentified anomalous phenomena in the western United States over two days in 2023: orange orbs repeatedly launching smaller red orbs, a large stationary glowing orb perched near a rock formation assessed by AARO at 12-18 meters diameter, a low-altitude object with red and white lights that moved laterally off-road with zero resistance and was later described to AARO as triangular, and a seemingly transparent kite-shaped object through which stars were faintly visible via night vision goggles. Although no technical sensor data is directly associated with the report, AARO conducted post-hoc measurements that revised witness estimates of distance and object size.

title: USPER Statement about UAP Sighting

object_types: oval shaped orange orb with white or yellow center
key_claims: A 'super-hot' orb was detected hovering at ground level via FLIR before travelling approximately 20 miles at a speed the pursuing helicopter could not match
The orb came within ten feet of the helicopter (CALL SIGN 1) before departing east at high speed
A swarm of lights too many to count was observed moving in all directions by both naked eye and NVG-equipped pilots
Repeated formations of four to five orbs flared up sequentially in horizontal patterns and then flared down in reverse order across multiple locations over approximately 30 minutes
The orbs appeared to break off from CALL SIGN 1 and pursue military aircraft operating in the area
novelty_signals: Senior US intelligence official as direct eyewitness, not just military pilot
Multi-sensor corroboration: FLIR, NVG, and naked eye all confirmed sightings simultaneously
Object splitting: single orb broke into two objects, then something emerged from the two and travelled in a different direction
Apparent interest in human assets: orb approached within 10 feet of helicopter and orbs appeared to pursue military aircraft
Coordinated swarm behavior: repeated sequential flare-up/flare-down pattern replicated across geographically separated locations over 30 minutes

parsed.summary: An FBI 302 documents a late-2025 incident in which a senior US intelligence official and helicopter crew conducted an aerial search of a mountainous area near a US military facility and encountered multiple UAP orbs detected on FLIR, NVG, and by naked eye — including a 'super-hot' orb that outran their helicopter over 20 miles and a recurring pattern of orb formations flaring up and down across the region. The orbs exhibited splitting behavior, approached within ten feet of the helicopter, and appeared to pursue military aircraft, with sightings spanning approximately 90 minutes across multiple locations.

title: NASA-UAP-D1, Apollo 12 Transcript, 1969

key_claims: LMP Alan Bean observed particles and flashes of light through the AOT that appeared to be escaping the Moon and moving rapidly toward the stars, not merely debris from the water boiler.
Bean reported an anomalous pulsing all-81s flash on both AGS DEDA registers at about one-fifth normal brilliance, pulsing every second.
Houston attributed the DEDA pulsing phenomenon to EMI, stating it had been observed during spacecraft testing at Bethpage.

CDR Pete Conrad reported that during a nightside pass, small bits and pieces were floating alongside the spacecraft, illuminated by the tracking light's flashing, and continued to be present even after the tracking light apparently burned out.
Houston's telemetry indicated the tracking light was still drawing current and functioning, contradicting the crew's visual observation that it had burned out.
novelty_signals: First-person astronaut observations of unidentified luminous phenomena near the lunar surface, reported in real time via air-to-ground voice transcription.
Distinction drawn by Bean between expected spacecraft debris and objects that appeared to be originating from or escaping the Moon itself.
Contradiction between ground telemetry (tracking light on) and crew visual observation (no flashing visible on nearby debris), suggesting an unexplained discrepancy.
parsed.summary: This Apollo 12 air-to-ground transcript excerpt documents two periods during which astronauts reported unidentified luminous phenomena: LMP Alan Bean observed flashes of light through the AOT that appeared to escape the Moon rather than originate from spacecraft systems, and CDR Pete Conrad noted debris illuminated by an apparently failed tracking light whose telemetry paradoxically showed it was still operating. Houston attributed some anomalies to EMI but the light phenomena near the lunar surface remained unexplained in the transcript.

title: NASA-UAP-D2, Apollo 17 Transcript, 1972

key_claims: CMP Ronald Evans observed very bright, jagged, angular fragments drifting and tumbling near the spacecraft during maneuver, some possibly 6 inches across, which LMP Schmitt compared to the Fourth of July.

CDR Eugene Cernan reported a distant bright object rotating rhythmically with alternating bright and dull flashes, which he emphasized was definitively not a nearby particle but something physical at great distance, estimated at 10-12 Earth diameters from Earth at roughly 11 o'clock position.

LMP Harrison Schmitt observed what he believed to be the S-IVB booster stage behind and above them relative to Earth, noting it had been visible for approximately 24 hours before he identified it as possibly the S-IVB.
CDR Cernan reported seeing bright flashes and streaks of light during sleep periods, including one described as a very bright spot flashing between his eyes like a train headlight.
LMP Schmitt reported seeing a bright flash on the lunar surface just north of Grimaldi crater, suggesting it could be a small impact event, and Houston agreed to check seismometer data.
novelty_signals: Astronaut crew observed unidentified phenomena across three distinct time periods spanning three days of the mission, indicating persistent and recurring anomalous observations.

CDR Cernan explicitly insisted a distant flashing object was not a nearby particle but something physical, with a distinctive dual-flash rotation pattern (bright then dull), and Houston attempted to triangulate its position using spacecraft attitude data.
A transient luminous event was observed on the lunar surface near Grimaldi crater, potentially an impact flash, representing a rare real-time witness observation of a lunar transient phenomenon.
Multiple crew members independently corroborated the observations, with Evans, Schmitt, and Cernan each providing distinct descriptions from different vantage points.
parsed.summary: This excerpt from the Apollo 17 air-to-ground transcript documents three periods of anomalous observations: bright tumbling fragments near the spacecraft during separation maneuvers on Day 1, a distant rhythmically flashing object tracked for hours on Day 2 that the crew debated could be the S-IVB stage or SLA panels, and a bright flash observed on the lunar surface near Grimaldi crater on Day 3. While some phenomena were tentatively attributed to spacecraft debris such as paint flakes, ice, or the S-IVB booster, the crew repeatedly emphasized that at least one distant object appeared to be a distinct physical body at considerable range.

title: NASA-UAP-D5, Apollo 17 Crew Debriefing for Science, 1973

key_claims: The Coma cluster cannot be held together by ionized hydrogen, as no red-shifted Lyman-alpha radiation was detected, leaving a mystery about what gravitationally binds it.

An anomalous UV spectrum resembling hot stars was observed at high galactic latitudes where no hot stars were in the field of view, possibly representing extragalactic radiation rather than reflected starlight.
Enormous amounts of Lyman-alpha hydrogen data were collected during Apollo 17, expected to clarify the picture of interstellar hydrogen streaming through the solar system.
The abnormally high dark current in the UV instrument did not interfere with the galactic pole observations.
The UV experiment observed the Earth's spectrum from outside the atmosphere.
novelty_signals: Unexplained UV background radiation at galactic poles with spectral characteristics inconsistent with the leading dust-reflection theory
Document is a science debriefing rather than a UAP sighting report, included in the PURSUE collection for its discussion of unexplained astronomical phenomena
parsed.summary: This excerpt from the Apollo 17 crew science debriefing on January 8, 1973 records Dick Henry discussing unexpected results from the ultraviolet astronomy experiment, including an anomalous UV background at high galactic latitudes that could not be fully explained by known stellar sources or dust reflection. The debriefing also covers the exclusion of ionized hydrogen as the binding mechanism for the Coma cluster and the collection of extensive Lyman-alpha data on interstellar hydrogen flowing through the solar system.
